definitions.explanation: Loanword from French, often implies a stylish or trendy establishment.

examples.japanese: {駅前|えきまえ}のカフェでコーヒーを{飲|の}んだ。
examples.english: I had coffee at the cafe in front of the station.

examples.japanese: この{街|まち}にはおしゃれなカフェがたくさんある。
examples.english: There are many stylish cafes in this town.

examples.japanese: {友達|ともだち}とカフェで{待|ま}ち{合|あ}わせした。
examples.english: I met up with a friend at a cafe.

notes:
カフェ is a loanword from French "café."

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
・カフェに{行|い}く - to go to a cafe
・カフェで{過|す}ごす - to spend time at a cafe
・カフェで{勉強|べんきょう}する - to study at a cafe

TYPES OF CAFES IN JAPAN:
・{猫|ねこ}カフェ - cat cafe
・ブックカフェ - book cafe
・メイドカフェ - maid cafe

USAGE:
カフェ implies a modern, stylish atmosphere, while {喫茶店|きっさてん} suggests a more traditional establishment.
